landing.heroBadge: AI dubbing with a director's chair
landing.heroSub: DubMaster is the first AI dubbing platform that puts you in the director's chair — with scene context, emotional controls, and a memory that learns your style.
landing.problemLeftTitle: Every other tool dubs your film and moves on.
landing.problemLeftBody: One-shot. No memory. No craft. The translation comes out, you take it or leave it — and if you don't speak the language, you have no idea whether what was said was right, wrong, or the complete opposite of what was meant.
landing.problemRightBody: Every correction you make is a directorial decision. Every decision gets remembered. Every future film benefits. That's not a tool — that's a studio.
landing.demoSub: Martial arts dubbing — the hardest test in the industry
landing.demoQuote: If it works on Ip Man, it works on anything.
landing.bollywoodBody: Get your film into any market without a dubbing studio budget.
landing.bollywoodStats: Full studio access on every plan
landing.indieBody: Reach global audiences without losing what makes your content yours.
landing.streamingBody: Dub across your entire catalog without growing the headcount.
landing.prosBody: A workspace that remembers every decision you've ever made.
landing.step1Desc: DubMaster transcribes, diarizes, and translates automatically — across 50+ languages. You get a full scene breakdown before you touch a single line.
landing.step2Desc: The Scene panel tells you what's happening, who's speaking, and what the line is doing dramatically — even if you don't speak the source language. You decide: accept the translation, correct it, or write your own.
landing.step3Desc: Every decision goes into your Rulebook — character voices, name mappings, tone rules, translation fixes. The next film you dub starts smarter than the last one ended.
landing.featuresTitle: The Full Studio, Open to Everyone
landing.feat1Desc: Zero-shot cloning preserves each actor's voice, accent, and delivery
landing.feat1Detail: Each detected speaker gets a cloned voice built from their own reference audio — timbre, accent, and delivery carry through. You can override casting per speaker, pick from the voice library, or supply custom voices.
landing.feat2Desc: emotion2vec scores every line against the original performance
landing.feat2Detail: Delivery directives let you control how a line is performed — angry, whispered, dismissive — and the QC pass scores the generated take against the original performance so drift is visible, not hidden.
landing.feat3Desc: Word-level timing analysis on every rendered segment
landing.feat3Detail: The QC Monitor measures audio-vs-audio offset in milliseconds per window — the metric that actually matters for perceived sync. Optional AI mouth re-animation is available as a paid add-on; see the lip-sync section below.
landing.feat4Desc: Lip-sync, emotion, timing, and translation findings — written up per segment
landing.feat4Detail: Every render produces a per-segment quality report: timing offset, emotional match, low-confidence spans, and flags you can review and fix inline.
landing.feat5Desc: Tuned for Cantonese and Mandarin; Japanese, Korean, Hindi, and more
landing.feat5Detail: The ASR stack is specifically tuned for Cantonese and Mandarin cinema — the hardest case — with full coverage across major target languages.
landing.feat6Desc: Upload and it runs — short clips finish in minutes
landing.feat6Detail: No sales calls, no studio queue. Upload, get a scene-broken transcript with speakers identified, and start directing within minutes.
landing.feat7Desc: Timeline editor, retranslation, voice casting, and review queue
landing.feat7Detail: A full cutting room: drag timing, rewrite lines, regenerate takes, compare Source vs Dubbed at the same playhead, and export when it's right.
landing.feat8Desc: Your corrections and directorial choices persist and shape future jobs
landing.feat8Detail: Name mappings, translation choices, character voices, tone rules — every decision you make is stored and applied to future jobs. Your studio gets smarter the more you use it.
landing.directorTitle: You don't need to speak Cantonese to know this line is wrong.
landing.directorBody: When a line is supposed to be a dismissal and the translation reads like an invitation — you'll catch it. Because DubMaster tells you exactly what's happening in the scene. The AI does the language. You do the direction.
landing.director3Desc: Who's talking and how they talk
landing.director4Desc: What the original performance felt like
landing.rulebookTitle: Professional dubbing studios have institutional knowledge built over decades.
landing.rulebookBody: Voice actors know the characters. Directors know the style. Writers know the idioms. That knowledge lives in people — and walks out the door when the project ends. DubMaster captures it digitally and makes it cumulative.
landing.rulebookList: Every name mapping. Every character voice. Every register rule. Every translation fix. Stored globally, applied to every future job. The longer you use DubMaster, the smarter it gets — about your films, your style, your creative voice.
landing.rulebookPunch: That's the moat. That's what no one-shot tool can replicate.
landing.lipsyncTitle: Why DubMaster doesn't include lip sync in the base render — and why that's a feature, not a limitation.
landing.lipsyncWhatTitle: What AI lip sync actually does
landing.lipsyncWhatBody: A lip sync engine regenerates the mouth region pixel-by-pixel using a generative model — predicting visemes and repainting the lower face to match, frame by frame. When it works, it's impressive. When it fails, it produces soft rectangles where a mouth used to be, identity drift, and desync on plosives. And failure is common — occlusion, rotation, low resolution, scene cuts, and complex lighting all break these engines. Most fail silently. Every failed frame still costs money.
landing.lipsyncOursBody: We align in the time domain — not the pixel domain. Your original face is never touched. Every dubbed line lands at the word-level onset of the original speech, with silence trimmed to 20ms. The QC Monitor measures real audio offset in milliseconds — a feedback loop, at no extra cost.
landing.lipsyncActionTitle: Built for the content that breaks every other tool
landing.lipsyncActionBody: Fast action, martial arts, high-energy scenes — where head rotation breaks face tracking, motion blur destroys the mouth region, and fast cuts leave less than a second of stable footage. A lip sync engine doesn't just underperform there; it fails on most frames, and you pay for every failed frame. DubMaster never touches the original face. Your actors stay your actors.
landing.lipsyncAddonTitle: For editors who want AI lip sync
landing.lipsyncAddonBody: We offer it — powered by Sync.Labs, priced at cost plus a small platform fee. But understand what you're buying: a generative pass that repaints the mouth region. It works on frontal, well-lit, high-resolution footage and struggles on everything else. Our recommendation: align manually and score with the QC monitor first. Most directors find they don't need more.
landing.lipsyncPunch: We give you the tool to get it right. We offer the option to go further. We're honest about which one most productions actually need.

landing.faq1Q: How is this different from Google Translate with voiceover?
landing.faq1A: We clone the original actor's voice and preserve their emotional delivery — every line is then scored for lip-sync and emotion. It's voice cloning plus an editing studio, not translation plus generic TTS.
landing.faq2Q: Can you really dub Cantonese martial arts films?
landing.faq2A: Yes — it's our primary test case. The pipeline separates Cantonese from Mandarin at the ASR stage, preserves fight-scene delivery, and scores the lip-sync timing on the result.
landing.faq3A: DubMaster aligns dubbed audio in the time domain — honest word-level timing, no face repainting, no generative artifacts. Optional AI lip sync is available as a paid add-on for footage it handles well; on fast action or angled shots we recommend the manual alignment instead.
landing.faq4A: It's fully self-serve — processing starts the moment you upload. Short clips finish in minutes; feature-length work takes hours of pipeline time. You edit while it runs.
landing.faq5A: Everyone gets the full timeline editor — no plan gate. Editing, retranslation, and review are always free; only the final render is metered.
landing.faq6A: 15 source languages and 14 target languages, with a pipeline specifically tuned for Cantonese and Mandarin cinema.
landing.testimonial: Translations can dilute a performance — or miss the point entirely. DubMaster changes that. With scene summaries, emotional controls, and full directorial oversight, you stay in command of every line, even in a language you don't speak.
landing.testimonialSub: Because the director always knows what the scene means.
